claims.text: The local catalog and selected early-1996 promo snapshot place the first CoroCoro glossy promo source slice on October 15, 1996, as the CoroCoro Comic November 1996 issue insert.
The selected snapshot lists two CoroCoro Comic November 1996 issue insert entries: Pikachu [Glossy] and Jigglypuff [Glossy].

This release sits five days before the official Japanese TCG launch date used elsewhere in the catalog. It is a magazine-insert doorway into the card game moment rather than a booster or deck product.

The same selected snapshot distinguishes the October 15, 1996 glossy CoroCoro Pikachu/Jigglypuff pair from a later November 30, 1996 non-glossy How-to-Play Pikachu/Jigglypuff pair. Glossy status and source route are therefore identity rails, not decoration.

The selected snapshot credits Pikachu [Glossy] to Ken Sugimori. The local row preserves that selected-source credit while retaining PokéCardex Keiji Kinebuchi as conflicting provider metadata, not as the accepted illustrator for this glossy row.
The local manual provider-path row credits Jigglypuff to Keiji Kinebuchi, source-scoped as selected/card-page metadata rather than physical-card proof.

The local catalog preserves Pikachu as a parent aggregate UPC row already hand-authored in the pilot source-set, and Jigglypuff as a manual provider-path row for the expected glossy CoroCoro counterpart; neither row is possession, authenticity, condition, or image-rights proof.

The first CoroCoro glossy promos matter because they show Pokémon becoming magazine-native at the exact edge of the TCG launch. Pikachu is already the face that can carry the franchise through a paper insert; Jigglypuff is the softer companion, proving that the early promotional machine was not just about power or rarity but about making the new card world feel friendly, shiny, and reachable.

Agents should preserve CoroCoro Comic November 1996 issue route, October 15 1996 date, glossy stock, row 001/002 identity, Pikachu Ken Sugimori preferred-source illustrator resolution from the existing pilot dossier, conflicting provider metadata, Jigglypuff Keiji Kinebuchi credit, Jigglypuff manual provider-path mode, and non-glossy How-to-Play non-equivalence before accepting a match.

narrative.why_it_matters: This slice feels like the magazine opening the door before the card game has even settled into public memory. Pikachu and Jigglypuff are not tournament trophies or deck staples here; they are glossy invitations. CoroCoro turns Pokémon into something a child can pull from an issue, hold up to the light, and understand immediately. Pikachu row 001 is already hand-authored in the pilot dossier, so this tranche keeps that illustrator-conflict rail visible while adding the release frame and Jigglypuff row 002. The agent has to be precise because the romance depends on it: glossy, October 1996, magazine route, row identity, and the Pikachu illustrator correction all belong to the story.
